study: qal/lsteer -- STEERED-INDUCTOR DRIVE FOR THE THREE-PHASE TRAPEZOID WAVE (mesh3 trap_tt92_d3, 5b9d05b). In every third one bank per phase-group RISES (R), one HOLDS (H), one FALLS (F). ONE inductor per 3-phase group is steered F -> L -> R; the holding bank is disconnected from L and clamped to a 1.65 V DC rail; a 0 V clamp catches the fallen bank over the last 4 ps of its fall. Question: can the 12x wave (129.0 ps standing eye, 12.0x per-level) be driven by a few steered inductors, at what L / I / N, at what energy. SPEED FIRST; energy REPORTED never gated.
written_before_any_deck: This file is the ONLY file in qal/lsteer/ at its mtime. Every topology choice, switch timing rule, L value, acceptance threshold and prediction below is fixed BEFORE the first lsteer deck exists and before lsteer.py exists. The instrument check (extract() of the committed trap_tt92_d3 .prn) and a Xyce syntax probe of the VSWITCH/inductor-IC semantics are the only runs permitted before this file; neither scores anything.

topology_FIXED.phase_nodes: pA, pB, pC per group; bank k hangs on p(ABC[(k-1) mod 3]) through 'VPHk phk pX 0' (0 V ammeter, same sign convention as the committed 'VPHk phsk 0': -I(VPHk) = current delivered to the bank).
topology_FIXED.third_schedule: third 0 (mod T): A=R, B=F, C=H  -> L steered B -> A.  third 1: B=R, C=F, A=H -> C -> B.  third 2: C=R, A=F, B=H -> A -> C.  Per phase the sequence is R,H,F,R,H,F: a fallen bank starts rising IMMEDIATELY, so the 0 V clamp can only be a pulse at the end of the fall.
topology_FIXED.inductor: ONE per 3-phase group: terminals lin (fed by the falling phase) and lout (feeding the rising phase); series R_L = 10 ohm (campaign convention) and a 1 ohm variant; standing current seeded with IC= (CCM) or 0 (DCM).
topology_FIXED.switches_per_group: 12 regardless of N: Sin_X (pX - lin, on while X falls), Sout_X (lout - pX, on while X rises), Shold_X (pX - vddh 1.65 V DC, on while X holds), Szero_X (pX - 0 V rail, pulse over the last 4 ps of X's fall, overlapping Sin_X: L then draws from the 0 V rail, no short to any other rail). The rising bank reaches ~1.65 V exactly at the third's end under current drive, so Shold engages with (near) NO step -- the mechanism the earlier clamp candidate B lacked.
topology_FIXED.break_before_make_BOTH_edges: closing control ramps over [t+0.2, t+0.5] ps, opening over [t-0.5, t-0.2] ps at every boundary t: 0.4 ps dead time, NO overlap of any two switches that would short vddh, 0 V, or two phase nodes. CHECKED by construction: at a boundary the only simultaneously-closing pairs are (Sin_new, Sout_new) across L, never across a rail.
topology_FIXED.dead_time_physics_ASSUMED: an inductor cannot be open-circuited: during the 0.4 ps dead time its current charges the terminal capacitances. C_t = 20 fF at lin and at lout (ASSUMED, labelled; a real 10-100 nH element's terminal/pad capacitance is larger). Expected terminal excursion I0 x 0.4 ps / 20 fF = 63 mV at 3.15 mA. Ideal rows use VSWITCH RON=0.05 ROFF=1e8 (ideal = BOUNDS). Real rows: 50 fF C_t (ASSUMED) because transistor gate edges are 2 ps.
topology_FIXED.switch_clamps_real_version: steering Sin/Sout: sg13_lv nMOS W=30 um L=0.13 um, gate PWL 0 <-> 2.174 V (= dV + Vtn, the campaign's binding spec; MEASURED Ron ~34 ohm at W=30 um), 2 ps edges, PLUS a TG variant (pMOS W=30 um bulk vddh, gate 1.65 <-> 0) because an nMOS at Vgs = 2.174 - 1.65 = 0.524 V = Vtn cannot carry 3 mA over the top ~100 mV of the swing -- PRE-STATED RISK: the nMOS-only steering row may stall the rise below ~1.55 V and hand the rest to the hold clamp (a step, costing margin). Shold: pMOS W=60 um bulk vddh gate 1.65 <-> 0 (passes 1.65 V with full overdrive; a 2.174 V nMOS would be at Vgs = Vtn there). Szero: nMOS W=10 um gate 0 <-> 1.65 V. Gate charge priced at the MEASURED 3.64-3.74 fC/um (use 3.7) x V_GH, cross-checked against the METERED up-edge gate charge in the deck; the committed 0.155 fC/um fit is NOT used (24x wrong).

regime_i_CCM_steered_standing_current.mechanism: I0 never reaches zero; at every boundary the switches re-route it to the next (F,R) pair with current flowing (hard switching, no ZCS). Bank rails ramp at dV/dt = I0/C(V): FASTER than the committed linear ramp early (C small while cells are off) and slower late -- a shape at least as kind to the receiver as the trapezoid (DERIVED from the measured 0.8 -> 2.9 mA demand ramp).
regime_i_CCM_steered_standing_current.self_sustaining_DERIVED_to_verify: V_L = V_F - V_R sweeps +1.65 -> -1.65 over a third: net volt-seconds ~0 so I0 is self-sustaining, and the loop is SELF-REGULATING: too much I0 overshoots both rails (V_L goes negative sooner, net volt-seconds negative, I0 falls); too little leaves both short (positive volt-seconds, I0 rises). Equilibrium: both swings fall short by the resistive drop I0 x R_total x (per-third average), i.e. the rising bank lands a few tens of mV BELOW 1.65 V (hold clamp steps it UP, from the DC rail -- that is where the resistive loss is paid) and the fallen bank a few tens of mV ABOVE 0 V. The equilibration time constant is L/R = 12 ns >> the 1.93 ns run, so the seed must be near equilibrium: a 3-point seed sweep (I0 = 2.8, 3.15, 3.5 mA at N=2) measures the drift per cycle and brackets the equilibrium by its sign change. VERIFIED if |drift| < 3 %/cycle at the best seed and the drift sign flips across the sweep.
regime_i_CCM_steered_standing_current.I0_expected: N x Q_rise / T_third = N x ~145 fC / 92 ps = N x 1.57 mA: 3.15 mA at N=2 (6-bank chain), 12.6 mA at N=8 (4 chain copies, 24 banks, one inductor).
regime_i_CCM_steered_standing_current.L_expected_and_the_sharing_law: ripple dI = (1/L) x integral(V_L > 0) = 1.65 V x 46 ps / 2 = 38 fWb / L, INDEPENDENT of N (rail waveforms do not change with N). 10 % ripple of N x 1.57 mA -> L = 38 fWb / (0.157 mA x N) = 240 nH / N: 120 nH at N=2, 30 nH at N=8. Sharing law to MEASURE: same absolute ripple (~0.31 mA) at N=2 and N=8 for L = 120 nH (10 % vs 2.5 %), and ~10 % again at N=8 with L = 30 nH.
regime_i_CCM_steered_standing_current.stored_energy: 0.5 L I0^2 = 595 fJ at N=2 (99 fJ per bank, N-invariant); resistive loss I0^2 R T = 27 fJ/cycle at 10 ohm (4.6 fJ/bank at N=2); at N=8 with R held at 10 ohm 438 fJ/cycle = 18 fJ/bank (R does not scale down with the 1/N L in the convention -- reported, with the 1 ohm variant).
regime_i_CCM_steered_standing_current.PREDICTION: value PASS at every bank; worst margin at commit >= 69.924 mV (expected within 10 % of the committed 509.67 mV: the hold is a stiff 1.65 V and the early rise is faster); overlap positive on every link; standing eye 129 +- 8 ps; arrival error at the hold clamp -20..-60 mV (short, from the resistive drop) at R_L = 10 ohm and < 15 mV at 1 ohm; terminal excursion <= 100 mV; ripple 10 +- 3 % at L = 120 nH, N = 2.

regime_ii_DCM_resonant_half_swing.mechanism: current starts and ends at zero every third; L sized so the F -> R series-LC half-cycle takes one third: t = pi sqrt(L C_ser). Switching at current zeros (no dead-time problem). Rail shape (1 - cos): SLOWER early than the linear ramp (sin current) -- the committed sine control (rise over 1.5 thirds) FAILED every d at T_third = 92 (sine_tt92_d3 worst margin -111.55 mV); the resonant rise here occupies ONE third, 1.5x faster than that sine, so it sits between the failed sine and the passing trapezoid.
regime_ii_DCM_resonant_half_swing.L_CORRECTED_before_any_deck: the task brief's 'L ~ 2.2 nH per bank pair' is an arithmetic slip: (92 ps / pi)^2 / 44 fF = (29.28 ps)^2 / 44 fF = 19.5 nH per bank pair (C_ser = 88 fF x 88 fF / 176 fF = 44 fF, C_bank = 145 fC / 1.65 V = 88 fF DERIVED). With N banks per phase C_ser = N x 44 fF -> L_DCM = 19.5 nH / N: 9.7 nH at N=2. Because C(V) is nonlinear and the hold current loads the swing, the actual half-period is MEASURED from the I(L) zero crossing and L is re-tuned (one re-probe iteration pre-authorised) -- zeros are never assumed.
regime_ii_DCM_resonant_half_swing.current_expected: half-sine carrying N x 145 fC in 92 ps: I_pk = pi Q / (2 t) = 2.47 mA per bank pair = 4.95 mA at N=2; I_rms over the third 3.5 mA; resistive loss 3 x I_rms^2 R x 92 ps = 34 fJ/cycle at 10 ohm (5.6 fJ/bank at N=2).
regime_ii_DCM_resonant_half_swing.arrival_shortfall_DERIVED: Z0 = sqrt(L / C_ser) = sqrt(9.7 nH / 88 fF) = 332 ohm, Q = Z0 / R = 33 at 10 ohm: swing amplitude factor exp(-pi / (2Q)) = 0.954 -> the rising bank lands at 1.65 x (1 + 0.954) / 2 = 1.612 V (-38 mV) and the falling bank at +38 mV; both corrected by the clamps from the DC rail. At 1 ohm: -4 mV.
regime_ii_DCM_resonant_half_swing.PREDICTION: value PASS probable; margin lower than CCM by the slower early rise (expected 300..450 mV, still >= 69.924); standing eye NARROWER than 129 ps (expected 105..125 ps); the P1 confirm is the test that decides it.

pick_PRE_STATED: (i) CCM. The constant-current rise is faster early than the trapezoid (nonlinear C), the hold is a stiff DC clamp, and the inductor is far from resonance so its value is uncritical; its costs are the standing current's I^2 R, the hard-switching dead-time excursion, and a LARGE L (120 nH at N=2 -- only the sharing law makes it buildable: 240 nH / N). DCM wins on L (9.7 nH / N... 19.5 nH / N) and on switching (at current zeros) but risks the sine-like early rise at the 92 ps design point.
N_sharing_measurement: N=2: the 6-bank chain, one inductor. N=8: FOUR identical copies of the chain (24 banks: banks 1..6, 7..12, 13..18, 19..24; each copy driven by its own ideal input word, identical pattern) on the SAME pA/pB/pC nodes, ONE inductor, same 12 switches. Scored: copy 1 (banks 1..6) through mesh3.extract(); copies 2..4 value-checked from their crest FINDs by the lsteer post-extractor. Rows: N=2 L=120 nH; N=8 L=120 nH (ripple should drop 4x); N=8 L=30 nH (ripple should return to ~10 %). The sharing law is CONFIRMED if the absolute ripple at L=120 nH agrees within 25 % between N=2 and N=8 and the N=8 L=30 nH ripple is within 25 % of the N=2 L=120 nH ripple.
energy_ledger_rules: per bank per cycle (T = 276 ps), bank-4-equivalent (mean over banks of the group, steady waves): (a) DC hold rail: 1.65 V x net charge drawn from vddh / (3N); (b) resistive: integral I_L^2 R_L dt + switch conduction loss (V x I over each switch, metered through 0 V ammeters) / (3N); (c) gate drive: metered up-edge gate charge x V_GH per switch per cycle, summed over the 12 switches / (3N), cross-checked vs 3.7 fC/um x W x V_GH; the meshdrv 1.33 chain tax reported alongside, not added; (d) 0 V rail: zero energy (V = 0) -- its charge is REPORTED; (e) inductor stored-energy drift 0.5 L (I_end^2 - I_start^2) per cycle reported (a non-zero value means the seed was off equilibrium and the DC rail is paying/receiving the difference). Energy balance cross-check: (a) - (e) must equal bank energy + (b) within 5 %. Ideal rows: (c) = 0 metered, priced at the fit as a RIDER. Compared against 240.292 fJ (mesh3 ideal rails) and 534 fJ (harmonic driver) -- REPORTED, NEVER GATED.
energy_PREDICTION: the hold charge alone is ~120 fC x 1.65 V = ~200 fJ/bank/cycle from the DC rail: the FLOOR of this construction is ~200-215 fJ/bank (below the 240.3 ledger only because the rise energy is recycled through L). Ideal-switch rows: ~210-230 fJ/bank at 10 ohm. Real-switch row at the 3.7 fC/um fit: 12 switches (6 x 30 um steering at 2.174 V, 3 x 60 um pMOS hold at 1.65 V, 3 x 10 um zero at 1.65 V) = ~(6x30x3.7x2.174 + 3x60x3.7x1.65 + 3x10x3.7x1.65) fJ / 6 banks = ~(1448 + 1099 + 183) / 6 = ~455 fJ/bank gate drive at N=2 (N-invariant: W scales with N), plus ~210 DC + ~30 resistive = ~700 fJ/bank: WORSE than the 534 fJ harmonic driver unless the clamp widths come down. TG steering doubles the steering gate bill. Pre-stated expectation: the ideal construction beats the ledger; the real-switch construction does NOT beat the harmonic driver on energy at the binding gate spec; the win, if any, is in L count/size (one inductor per 3N banks) and in speed (the eye).

acceptance.A_value: ALL banks, waves 2..4: last-level word bit-correct vs the receiver's instantaneous trip at the raw-validity midpoint (mesh3 A).
acceptance.B_eye: links 1..5, waves 2..4, both polarities: margin at the commit sample >= 69.924 mV.
acceptance.D_standing_eye: REPORTED vs 129.0 ps (asymptotic width, erosion sign SUSTAINS required for a PASS row).
acceptance.E_arrival: REPORTED: rail at the instant before the hold clamp closes minus 1.65 V, and rail at the instant before the zero clamp closes; CCM self-sustain drift %/cycle; DCM measured zero-crossing vs the third's end.
acceptance.PASS: A and B and C and SUSTAINS on P0; the BEST row is confirmed on P1 (the killing mixed word).
acceptance.verdict_rule: 'can be constructed with inductors in principle' = any IDEAL-switch row PASSES (a BOUND). 'buildable' = a REAL-switch row PASSES; its energy is reported against 240.3 and 534 fJ without gating.
